title: Chicken Adobo
summary: Tender chicken braised in soy sauce, vinegar, garlic and bay leaves until glossy and deeply savoury.

stages.title: Marinate the chicken
steps: Combine soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, bay leaves and peppercorns in a bowl.
Turn chicken in the marinade and refrigerate for 20 minutes; reserve the liquid.

stages.title: Brown the chicken
steps: Heat oil in a deep frying pan over medium-high heat and lift chicken from marinade.
Brown skin-side down first for 5 minutes, then turn and cook another 3–5 minutes.

stages.title: Braise gently
steps: Pour reserved marinade and water into the pan and bring to a full boil before lowering heat.
Cover and simmer 20 minutes, then uncover and reduce 10 minutes until glossy and chicken reaches 75°C.

stages.title: Balance and serve
steps: Taste the sauce; add a splash of water if too salty or a little vinegar if too rich.
Serve chicken and its reduced sauce over hot steamed rice.

tips: Do not stir immediately after adding vinegar; allow the sauce to come to a boil.
Use bone-in thighs for more flavour, allowing extra cooking time.
variations: Add 1 tsp brown sugar if you prefer a sweeter balance.
Use coconut vinegar for a traditional regional variation.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Beef Rendang
summary: Slow-cooked beef infused with coconut milk, lemongrass, galangal and spices until dark and caramelised.

stages.title: Blend the spice paste
steps: Blend shallots, garlic, ginger, chillies and coriander with a splash of water until coarse.
Pat beef dry and cut into equal 4 cm cubes for even cooking.

stages.title: Fry the aromatics
steps: Heat oil in a heavy pot and fry the paste over medium heat until fragrant and darker.
Add lemongrass and lime leaves, stirring until their aromas release.

stages.title: Slow-cook the beef
steps: Add beef, coconut milk and salt; bring to a simmer and lower the heat.
Cook uncovered or partly covered for 2 hours, stirring more often as liquid reduces, until beef is tender.

stages.title: Reduce to a coating
steps: Continue cooking gently until the coconut mixture thickens and clings to the meat.
Stir frequently to prevent burning and stop when the paste is deep brown and the beef pulls apart easily.

tips: Rendang is a slow reduction, not a soupy curry.
Stir frequently during the final 30 minutes as coconut solids can scorch.
variations: Add a pinch of chilli flakes for extra heat.
Finish with fresh herbs or citrus where appropriate.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Classic French Quiche Lorraine
summary: Buttery pastry filled with smoky bacon, Gruyère and a delicate savoury egg custard.

stages.title: Blind-bake pastry
steps: Heat oven to 190°C conventional and press pastry into a 23 cm tart tin.
Line with baking paper and weights, bake 15 minutes, then remove weights and bake 5 minutes more.

stages.title: Cook bacon
steps: Fry bacon in a dry pan over medium heat until lightly golden and fat renders.
Drain on kitchen paper so the filling does not become greasy.

stages.title: Make the custard
steps: Whisk eggs, cream, milk, nutmeg and pepper until just combined, avoiding excessive foam.
Scatter bacon and cheese evenly over the baked pastry case.

stages.title: Bake and rest
steps: Pour custard into the tart and bake at 180°C for 30–35 minutes until edges are set and centre gently wobbles.
Rest 10 minutes before slicing so the custard firms without drying.

tips: Avoid overbaking: the centre should still have a slight wobble.
Classic Lorraine often omits cheese; Gruyère is a popular addition.
variations: Add a pinch of chilli flakes for extra heat.
Finish with fresh herbs or citrus where appropriate.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Japanese Teriyaki Chicken Donburi
summary: Tender teriyaki-glazed chicken over steamed rice with spring onions and sesame.

stages.title: Cook the rice
steps: Rinse rice until the water runs nearly clear and cook with the packet-specified amount of water.
Rest covered for 10 minutes after cooking, then fluff with a fork.

stages.title: Mix the glaze
steps: Stir soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Slice spring onions thinly and keep the green tops for serving.

stages.title: Sear chicken
steps: Heat oil in a skillet and cook thighs over medium-high heat for 5–6 minutes each side.
Check the thickest part reaches 75°C before removing excess rendered fat.

stages.title: Glaze and serve
steps: Pour sauce into the pan and simmer, turning chicken, until glossy and lightly thickened.
Slice chicken and spoon over rice with pan glaze, spring onions and sesame seeds.

tips: Pat the chicken thighs dry before they hit the pan: surface moisture steams the meat instead of searing it, so you miss the browned edges that give the glaze something to cling to.
Spoon off excess rendered fat before adding the sauce, as thigh fat will keep the glaze from thickening and leave it greasy rather than glossy.
Add the sauce only once the chicken is cooked through and simmer briefly: the sugar and mirin caramelise fast and can turn bitter and sticky if they reduce for too long on high heat.
variations: Swap the chicken for salmon fillets, searing skin-side down for about 4 minutes, then flipping and glazing for the last 2 minutes so the fish stays moist.
Make it a veggie-loaded bowl by adding steamed broccolini and quick-pickled cucumber on the side, and top with a soft-boiled egg for extra protein for the kids.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Korean Beef Bulgogi
summary: Thinly sliced beef marinated in soy, pear, garlic and sesame, quickly seared until caramelised.

stages.title: Make the marinade
steps: Mix soy sauce, sugar, grated pear, garlic, ginger and sesame oil until combined.
Toss with thinly sliced beef and refrigerate for at least 20 minutes.

stages.title: Prepare vegetables
steps: Slice onion into fine half-moons and cut spring onions into 4 cm pieces.
Drain excess marinade from beef so it sears rather than boils.

stages.title: Sear in batches
steps: Heat a large skillet until very hot and add a little neutral oil.
Cook beef in small batches for 2–3 minutes per side until browned and fully cooked.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Return beef to pan with onion and spring onion, tossing until onion softens slightly.
Serve immediately with rice and optional lettuce leaves.

tips: Freeze the beef for about 30 minutes before slicing so you can cut it paper-thin; thin slices cook in seconds and stay tender.
Grated pear contains enzymes that tenderise the beef, but marinate for no more than 4 hours or the meat turns mushy.
Cook in small batches in a very hot pan; crowding drops the temperature so the beef steams and turns grey instead of caramelising.
variations: Swap the beef for thinly sliced pork shoulder (dwaeji bulgogi) and add 1 tbsp gochujang to the marinade for a spicy, sticky version.
Serve as lettuce wraps (ssam) with steamed rice, kimchi and ssamjang, so everyone builds their own at the table.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Moroccan Chicken Tagine with Olives
summary: Chicken gently braised with olives, preserved lemon and aromatic Moroccan spices.

stages.title: Brown chicken
steps: Heat olive oil in a casserole over medium-high heat and season chicken lightly.
Brown thighs on both sides, then transfer to a plate without cooking through.

stages.title: Soften aromatics
steps: Lower heat and cook onion until softened, scraping up browned bits.
Add garlic, ginger, turmeric and cumin and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.

stages.title: Braise gently
steps: Return chicken with stock, bring to a simmer and cover.
Cook 30–35 minutes until tender and the thickest part reaches 75°C.

stages.title: Add preserved lemon
steps: Rinse preserved lemon and finely slice the rind; discard excess pulp and seeds.
Stir in olives and lemon rind, simmer uncovered until sauce lightly thickens, then finish with coriander.

tips: Brown the thighs well before braising: the caramelised bits left in the pot dissolve into the stock and give the sauce a deeper, roasted flavour.
Rinse the preserved lemon and use only the rind, because the salty pulp can make the whole tagine harsh and over-salted, especially once the sauce reduces.
Add the olives and lemon rind only at the end, as long simmering turns the olives bitter and dulls the bright, fragrant lemon flavour.
variations: Swap the green olives for a handful of dried apricots or prunes and add a cinnamon stick with the spices for a sweeter, more Fez-style tagine.

Make it with lamb shoulder pieces instead of chicken, extending the covered braise to about 1.5 hours until the meat is fork-tender, and stir through a can of drained chickpeas for the last 15 minutes.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Italian Chicken Cacciatore
summary: Rustic chicken simmered with tomatoes, peppers, mushrooms and herbs in a savoury Italian sauce.

stages.title: Brown chicken
steps: Season thighs with salt and pepper and brown in olive oil over medium-high heat.
Turn once to colour both sides, then set aside on a plate.

stages.title: Cook vegetables
steps: Add sliced onion, capsicum and mushrooms to the same pan.
Cook until mushrooms release their liquid and begin to brown, then add minced garlic and oregano.

stages.title: Deglaze and simmer
steps: Pour in wine, scraping the base, and simmer for 3 minutes before adding tomatoes and stock.
Return chicken, cover loosely and simmer gently until chicken reaches 75°C.

stages.title: Reduce and finish
steps: Uncover and simmer until sauce coats a spoon rather than pooling thinly.
Taste for salt and acidity, then serve with polenta or crusty bread.

tips: Brown the thighs hard and leave the browned bits in the pan: when the wine hits them they dissolve into the sauce and give it a deeper, meatier flavour than simmering alone.
Let the mushrooms release their liquid and colour before adding garlic. Garlic burns quickly and turns bitter, and wet mushrooms will steam rather than brown if the pan is crowded.

Use skin-on, bone-in thighs if you can. The bone and fat keep the meat tender through the long simmer and add body to the sauce, but spoon off excess fat before reducing so the sauce doesn't turn greasy.
variations: Swap the red wine for dry white wine and add a strip of lemon peel and a few green olives for a lighter, brinier cacciatore.
Make it a pasta bake: shred the cooked chicken off the bone, toss it through the reduced sauce with cooked rigatoni, top with mozzarella and bake until bubbling.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Mexican Chicken Enchiladas Rojas
summary: Soft tortillas rolled around spiced chicken and baked under red chilli sauce and melted cheese.

stages.title: Prepare filling
steps: Heat oil in a skillet and soften diced onion until translucent.
Stir in shredded chicken and 100 ml enchilada sauce, heating until steaming hot.

stages.title: Soften tortillas
steps: Heat tortillas briefly in a dry skillet so they roll without cracking.
Spread a thin layer of sauce across the base of a baking dish.

stages.title: Fill and roll
steps: Divide chicken mixture between tortillas, roll tightly and arrange seam-side down.
Pour remaining sauce over the top and scatter with grated cheese.

stages.title: Bake and serve
steps: Bake at 190°C conventional for 18–22 minutes until bubbling and hot throughout.
Rest 5 minutes, then top with sour cream and coriander.

tips: Warm the corn tortillas in a dry pan before rolling: cold corn tortillas crack and split, while warmed ones turn pliable and hold the filling.
Spread a thin layer of sauce on the base of the dish first so the tortillas don't stick or scorch, and the bottom ones soften into the sauce rather than drying out.
Shred the cheese yourself from a block of Monterey Jack: pre-grated bags contain anti-caking agents that stop it melting into a smooth, bubbly blanket.
variations: Swap the chicken for a filling of black beans and roasted sweet potato with the same red sauce for a vegetarian version that still holds together when rolled.
Make enchiladas verdes by replacing the red sauce with salsa verde and topping with crumbled queso fresco instead of the Monterey Jack, for a tangier, lighter finish.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Chinese Char Siu Pork
summary: Sticky Cantonese-style roast pork glazed with honey, hoisin and fragrant five-spice.
ingredients: 800 g pork shoulder, cut into strips

stages.title: Mix marinade
steps: Whisk hoisin, soy, honey, wine, five-spice, garlic and sugar into a smooth glaze.
Reserve 2 tablespoons in a separate clean bowl for basting before adding raw meat.

stages.title: Marinate pork
steps: Coat pork strips thoroughly and refrigerate at least 30 minutes, ideally overnight.
Arrange on a rack above a foil-lined roasting tray so hot air circulates.

stages.title: Roast the pork
steps: Heat oven to 200°C conventional and roast 25 minutes, turning halfway.
Brush with reserved clean glaze and continue cooking until pork is safely cooked and tender.

stages.title: Caramelise and rest
steps: Increase oven to 220°C for a few minutes until edges become sticky and lightly charred.
Rest pork 5 minutes before slicing across the grain.

tips: Use pork shoulder (or scotch fillet) rather than lean loin: the marbling bastes the meat as it roasts, so the strips stay juicy instead of drying out under the high heat.
Roast on a rack over a foil-lined tray with a splash of water in the tray: air circulates so the glaze caramelises on all sides, and the water stops the dripping sugars from burning and smoking.

Keep the reserved glaze separate from the raw meat and only brush it on for the final stage: it gives a fresh, glossy layer of stickiness that the first coat loses to the oven, and it avoids cross-contamination.
variations: Swap the pork shoulder for chicken thigh fillets and cut the roasting time to about 20 minutes: the same glaze gives a quicker, milder char siu that suits younger kids.
Add 1 tbsp of red fermented bean curd to the marinade for a more traditional Cantonese flavour and a deeper reddish colour, without needing food dye.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Indian Butter Chicken
summary: Tender tandoori-spiced chicken in a buttery tomato cream sauce with warming spices.

stages.title: Marinate chicken
steps: Mix yoghurt, half the garam masala, paprika, half the garlic and salt.
Coat chicken and refrigerate for at least 20 minutes before cooking.

stages.title: Sear the chicken
steps: Heat 20 g butter in a wide pan and cook chicken in batches until lightly coloured.
Remove to a plate; the chicken will finish cooking in the sauce.

stages.title: Build the sauce
steps: Add remaining butter, garlic, ginger and tomato paste; stir for 1 minute.
Add passata and remaining garam masala, simmer 15 minutes and blend carefully if a silky sauce is preferred.

stages.title: Finish gently
steps: Return chicken and juices, simmer until chicken reaches 75°C.
Reduce heat, stir in cream and taste for salt before serving with rice.

tips: Use thighs rather than breast: the extra fat keeps the chicken juicy through the sear and the long simmer, and it won't turn stringy like breast can.
Sear the chicken in batches so the pan stays hot; crowding it steams the meat, and you lose the browned bits that add depth to the sauce.
Stir the cream in off a low heat, not a rolling simmer, so the sauce stays smooth and doesn't split from the acidity of the passata.
variations: Swap the cream for coconut cream for a dairy-free-style sauce with a slightly sweeter, rounder flavour.
Make it with 600 g firm paneer or peeled prawns instead of chicken, adding prawns in the last 4 minutes so they stay tender.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Spanish Chicken and Chorizo Rice
summary: One-pan saffron-tinted rice with juicy chicken, smoky chorizo and sweet peppers.

stages.title: Brown the proteins
steps: Heat olive oil in a wide pan and brown seasoned chicken pieces.
Add sliced chorizo and cook until its paprika-red oil releases, then transfer both to a plate.

stages.title: Build the rice base
steps: Soften onion and capsicum in the same pan, then add garlic and smoked paprika.
Stir in tomatoes and rice, coating grains in the fragrant oil.

stages.title: Simmer without stirring
steps: Pour in hot stock infused with saffron and return chicken and chorizo.
Simmer gently without stirring for 18–22 minutes, adding a little hot water only if rice dries before tender.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Check chicken reaches 75°C and rice is cooked; cover off the heat for 5 minutes.
Fluff only lightly at serving to preserve any golden crust underneath.

tips: Brown the chicken thighs skin-side down first and leave them alone: the rendered fat and caramelised bits left in the pan flavour the rice, so don't wipe it out.
Use raw cooking chorizo, not the dry cured kind: it releases paprika-red oil that stains and seasons every grain, while cured chorizo stays firm and gives far less flavour to the rice.
Don't stir once the stock is in: leaving the rice undisturbed lets the base form a golden, crisp socarrat crust, whereas stirring releases starch and makes it creamy like risotto.
variations: Swap the chicken for 400 g of peeled raw prawns and 200 g of firm white fish, stirring them in for the last 8 minutes of simmering so they stay tender, and use fish or seafood stock for a seafood paella style.
Make it vegetarian by replacing the chicken and chorizo with 1 sliced zucchini, 1 drained can of chickpeas and an extra teaspoon of smoked paprika, and use vegetable stock.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Turkish Lamb Köfte
summary: Chargrilled lamb kofta with cumin, garlic and parsley, served with flatbread and yoghurt.

stages.title: Mix and shape
steps: Squeeze excess liquid from grated onion and mix with lamb, garlic, spices, parsley and salt.
Knead briefly until mixture holds together, then form 12 short oval patties.

stages.title: Chill the patties
steps: Place shaped köfte on a tray and refrigerate 15 minutes to firm.
Heat a griddle or heavy pan while the patties chill.

stages.title: Cook thoroughly
steps: Brush köfte lightly with oil and grill over medium-high heat, turning every few minutes.
Cook until browned and the centre reaches 75°C for minced meat.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Rest köfte for 3 minutes while warming flatbreads.
Serve with chopped tomato, cucumber and a yoghurt sauce.

tips: Squeeze the grated onion in your fist or a clean tea towel before mixing; the excess juice makes the mince wet and the köfte can slump or fall apart on the grill.
Chill the shaped patties for the full 15 minutes so the lamb fat firms up and the köfte hold their shape instead of sticking to the grates.
Use a probe thermometer and pull the köfte at 75°C: minced lamb must be cooked through, and resting for 3 minutes lets the juices settle so they stay moist.
variations: Swap half the lamb for beef mince for a milder, more budget-friendly köfte that still browns well.
Thread the mixture onto flat metal skewers to make şiş köfte, then serve with charred tomatoes and capsicum and a sumac onion salad.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Vietnamese Beef Pho
summary: Fragrant beef broth with rice noodles, tender beef, fresh herbs and warming spices.

stages.title: Char the aromatics
steps: Char onion halves and ginger under a hot grill until edges blacken lightly.
Rinse charred surfaces briefly and toast whole spices in a dry pan until fragrant.

stages.title: Build the broth
steps: Cover bones with water, boil for 5 minutes, drain and rinse bones and pot to remove impurities.
Add fresh water, aromatics and spices and simmer gently for 2 hours, skimming foam as needed.

stages.title: Strain and season
steps: Strain broth through a fine sieve and discard solids and spent spices.
Season with fish sauce and a little salt until savoury but not overly salty.

stages.title: Assemble bowls
steps: Soak or boil noodles as directed, divide between warm bowls and top with thin beef slices.
Pour vigorously boiling broth over beef, ensuring it cooks through, and serve with herbs, sprouts and lime.

tips: Parboil the bones for 5 minutes and rinse them before the long simmer. This pulls out the blood and impurities that would otherwise cloud the broth and leave a scummy, muddy flavour.

Slice the steak as thinly as you can, ideally after 20 minutes in the freezer to firm it up. Paper-thin slices cook through instantly when the boiling broth hits them and stay tender instead of going grey and chewy.
Keep the broth at a gentle simmer rather than a rolling boil. Hard boiling emulsifies the fat and collagen into the liquid, making the pho cloudy and greasy rather than clear and clean-tasting.
variations: Swap the steak for chicken pho (pho ga): use a whole chicken or chicken carcasses instead of beef bones, simmer for about 1 hour, then shred the meat to top the bowls.
Make a vegetarian version with a broth of charred onion, ginger, daikon, dried shiitake mushrooms and the same spices, then top with fried tofu and bok choy in place of the beef.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Italian Pasta alla Norma
summary: Silky aubergine in a tangy tomato and basil sauce tossed with pasta and salty ricotta salata.

stages.title: Brown aubergine
steps: Salt aubergine cubes lightly, pat dry and toss with 2 tablespoons olive oil.
Roast at 220°C for 18 minutes until golden and soft, turning halfway.

stages.title: Make tomato sauce
steps: Warm remaining oil in a skillet and gently cook sliced garlic until fragrant but not brown.
Add tomatoes and simmer 12–15 minutes, breaking them up with a spoon.

stages.title: Cook pasta
steps: Boil rigatoni in well-salted water until just al dente.
Reserve a cup of pasta water before draining.

stages.title: Combine and serve
steps: Toss pasta, tomato sauce and aubergine together, loosening with pasta water.
Fold in torn basil and finish with grated ricotta salata.

tips: Salting the aubergine and patting it dry draws out moisture, so the cubes roast to golden and creamy instead of steaming and turning spongy.
Toss the aubergine in oil before roasting so every cube is coated; aubergine soaks up oil like a sponge, and an even coating browns it evenly without needing extra oil in the tray.
Keep a cup of the starchy pasta water and add it splash by splash when tossing; it loosens the thick tomato sauce and helps it cling to the ridges of the rigatoni.
variations: Pasta alla Norma bake: toss everything together, top with grated mozzarella and extra Parmesan, and bake at 200°C for 15 minutes until bubbling and golden. Good for making ahead for the family.
Smoky version: add 1 tsp smoked paprika to the aubergine before roasting and stir 2 tbsp drained capers and a few chopped olives into the sauce for a salty, punchy flavour.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: American BBQ Pulled Pork
summary: Slow-smoked-style shredded pork with a sweet, tangy barbecue glaze and crisp edges.

stages.title: Season the pork
steps: Pat shoulder dry and rub all over with sugar, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder and salt.
Place in a snug lidded roasting dish and pour apple juice around, not over, the meat.

stages.title: Slow roast
steps: Cover tightly and roast at 150°C conventional for about 4 hours.
Check occasionally that liquid remains in the base and cook until pork is fork-tender.

stages.title: Shred and sauce
steps: Rest pork 10 minutes, remove excess fat and shred with two forks.
Mix with warm cooking juices and BBQ sauce until moist but not soupy.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Toast burger buns cut-side down until lightly golden.
Pile in pulled pork and add coleslaw if desired.

tips: Pour the apple juice around the pork, not over it, so the spice rub stays intact and builds a proper bark instead of washing into the liquid.
Leave the pork covered for the whole cook: a tight lid traps steam, which melts the collagen in the shoulder and keeps the meat moist and fork-tender.
Toss the shredded pork in the warm cooking juices before adding the BBQ sauce, as the fat-rich juices carry flavour through the meat and stop the sauce tasting sugary and flat.
variations: Swap the BBQ sauce for a Carolina-style mix of apple cider vinegar, a little brown sugar and chilli flakes for a tangier, thinner finish, and serve with crunchy slaw on the bun.
Make it in a slow cooker: cook on low for 8 hours, then spread the shredded pork on a tray, brush with sauce and grill for 5 minutes to get crisp edges.
storage: Cool promptly; refrigerate pulled pork up to 3 days or freeze up to 3 months. Reheat until steaming hot.

title: French Beef Bourguignon
summary: Beef slowly braised in red wine with mushrooms, carrots and pearl onions until fork-tender.

stages.title: Brown beef and bacon
steps: Pat beef dry, season, then brown in batches in olive oil in a heavy casserole.
Remove beef and fry bacon until golden, leaving some fat in the pot.

stages.title: Build the braise
steps: Soften chopped onion and carrots, then add garlic and flour and stir 1 minute.
Pour in wine slowly, scraping the base, then add stock, thyme, beef and bacon.

stages.title: Slow cook
steps: Cover and cook at 160°C conventional for about 2½ hours until beef is fork-tender.
Check liquid halfway and add a little stock if it becomes dry.

stages.title: Finish mushrooms
steps: Brown mushrooms separately in a hot skillet to prevent them steaming.
Stir into the stew for the last 10 minutes and adjust seasoning before serving.

tips: Pat the beef dry and brown it in batches: crowding the pot makes the meat steam rather than sear, and you lose the browned base that gives the sauce its depth.
Use a wine you'd happily drink, such as a Pinot Noir or Burgundy-style red. The wine reduces over the long braise, so any harshness or sourness gets concentrated in the sauce.
Brown the mushrooms separately in a hot pan and add them near the end. Cooked in the stew for hours they turn soggy and grey, but this keeps their texture and flavour.
variations: Swap the beef chuck for beef cheeks or oxtail. Their extra collagen makes a silkier, more sticky sauce, but allow an extra 30 to 45 minutes of braising.
Make it a Beef and Guinness-style stew by replacing the red wine with a dark stout and adding a spoonful of tomato paste. Serve with mash or crusty bread for a heartier, maltier dish.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Sicilian Caponata
summary: Sweet-and-sour Sicilian aubergine with tomatoes, celery, olives, capers and vinegar.

stages.title: Brown aubergine
steps: Dice aubergine into 2 cm cubes and toss with half the olive oil.
Roast at 220°C until golden and soft, turning once.

stages.title: Soften vegetables
steps: Heat remaining oil in a wide pan and cook diced onion and celery over medium heat.
Stir occasionally until tender but not browned.

stages.title: Build sweet-sour sauce
steps: Add tomatoes, olives, rinsed capers, vinegar and sugar.
Simmer gently until tomatoes thicken and flavours balance, adjusting vinegar or sugar a little at a time.

stages.title: Combine and rest
steps: Fold roasted aubergine through the sauce without crushing the pieces.
Rest at least 10 minutes and finish with parsley; serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: Roast the aubergine separately instead of frying it in the sauce: the dry oven heat browns the cubes without them soaking up excess oil, so they stay meaty rather than greasy.
Rinse the capers well before adding them, because brine-packed capers are very salty and will otherwise overpower the delicate sweet-sour balance as the sauce reduces.
Make it a day ahead if you can: resting overnight in the fridge lets the vinegar mellow and the sugar soak into the aubergine, so the flavour is rounder and the sweet-sour balance more settled.
variations: Stir through 2 tbsp toasted pine nuts and 2 tbsp sultanas at the end for a more traditional Palermo-style caponata with extra sweetness and crunch.
Turn it into a main by tossing it through cooked short pasta such as rigatoni and topping with toasted breadcrumbs and shaved ricotta salata.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in a covered container up to 4 days. Serve cold or reheat gently; do not leave at room temperature for extended periods.

title: Greek Lemon Potatoes
summary: Roast potatoes infused with lemon, oregano, garlic and olive oil until golden and tender.

stages.title: Cut and season
steps: Heat oven to 210°C conventional and cut potatoes into even thick wedges.
Toss with olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, oregano and salt in a roasting dish.

stages.title: Add stock and roast
steps: Pour stock around potatoes and spread wedges in a single layer.
Roast 35–40 minutes, turning once, until tender and most liquid has evaporated.

stages.title: Crisp the edges
steps: Increase oven to 230°C and turn potatoes to expose pale surfaces.
Roast a further 10–15 minutes until golden, adding only a splash of water if sticking.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Spoon pan juices over the potatoes and taste for salt.
Serve immediately with extra lemon wedges.

tips: Use waxy potatoes such as Desiree or Dutch cream: they hold their shape while absorbing the lemon stock, whereas floury varieties like Russet Burbank can collapse into mush.
Cut wedges to an even thickness so they all finish tender at the same time and the stock reduces evenly around them.
Turn the potatoes so their pale, damp surfaces face up for the final high-heat blast; the surfaces that sat in the liquid are the ones that need to dry out and brown.
variations: Swap half the potatoes for sweet potato wedges and add them for the second roasting stage, since they cook faster and their sweetness balances the sharp lemon.
Stir 1 tbsp of Dijon mustard into the lemon and oil mixture for a tangy, slightly creamy coating, and scatter crumbled feta over the top just before serving.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Japanese Sesame Spinach (Goma-ae)
summary: Blanched spinach tossed with a delicate sesame dressing, soy and a touch of sweetness.

stages.title: Blanch spinach
steps: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and blanch spinach for 30–45 seconds until wilted.
Transfer immediately to cold water to stop cooking and preserve colour.

stages.title: Drain thoroughly
steps: Squeeze spinach gently in handfuls to remove excess water.
Cut into 4 cm lengths so the dressing coats evenly.

stages.title: Make sesame dressing
steps: Grind sesame seeds roughly in a mortar, leaving some texture.
Mix with soy sauce, sugar and mirin until the sugar dissolves.

stages.title: Dress and serve
steps: Toss spinach with sesame dressing just before serving.
Taste and add a few drops of soy sauce if needed.

tips: Squeeze the blanched spinach firmly but gently: any water left in the leaves thins the dressing and leaves it watery and pale rather than clinging to the spinach.
Grind the sesame seeds only until roughly crushed, as cracking the seeds releases their oils and aroma, while a few whole seeds left in give the dish a nutty texture.
Dress the spinach just before serving, because the salt and soy draw moisture out of the leaves and the dressing turns sloppy if it sits.
variations: Swap the spinach for blanched green beans or asparagus spears, which stay crisp and hold the thick sesame dressing well.
Make a creamier dressing by stirring in 1 tsp of tahini or Japanese sesame paste, which gives a richer, smoother coating and suits kids who prefer less texture.
storage: Refrigerate promptly up to 2 days. Serve chilled; do not freeze.

title: Indian Cucumber Raita
summary: Cool yoghurt mixed with cucumber, cumin and mint to balance spicy curries.

stages.title: Prepare cucumber
steps: Grate cucumber coarsely and squeeze gently to remove watery juices.
Keep some texture rather than blending it into a purée.

stages.title: Season yoghurt
steps: Whisk yoghurt until smooth, then add cumin, salt and lemon juice.
Taste for tang and adjust seasoning before adding cucumber.

stages.title: Combine and chill
steps: Fold cucumber, mint and coriander into yoghurt.
Refrigerate at least 10 minutes to let flavours meld.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Stir once before serving and scatter over a pinch of cumin.
Serve cold alongside spicy curries or flatbread.

tips: Squeeze the grated cucumber in your hands or a clean tea towel before folding it in, because the water it releases will thin the yoghurt and leave a watery pool in the bowl.
Dry-roast whole cumin seeds in a pan for about a minute and grind them fresh, as the toasty, nutty flavour is much stronger than pre-ground cumin and stands up to hot curries.
Use full-fat Greek-style yoghurt if you can, since its thick body holds up against the cucumber's moisture and stays creamy for the full two days in the fridge.
variations: Boondi raita: stir in 1/2 cup of soaked boondi (tiny fried chickpea-flour pearls) for a crunchy, savoury texture that kids tend to love.
Tomato and onion raita: swap the cucumber for finely diced ripe tomato and 1/2 a finely diced red onion, and add a pinch of ground coriander for a sharper, more robust side.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container up to 2 days; stir before serving. Do not freeze.

title: Mexican Refried Beans
summary: Creamy mashed pinto beans cooked with onion, garlic and savoury Mexican spices.
ingredients: 2 x 400 g tins pinto beans, drained

stages.title: Soften onion
steps: Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook finely diced onion until translucent.
Add minced garlic and cumin, stirring for 30 seconds until fragrant.

stages.title: Simmer beans
steps: Add drained beans and 150 ml water or stock, scraping the pan.
Simmer gently until beans are hot and begin to soften further.

stages.title: Mash to texture
steps: Mash beans with a potato masher, leaving some pieces intact.
Add more liquid a little at a time until creamy and spoonable, not stiff.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Season with salt and a squeeze of lime juice.
Serve warm with tacos, rice or grilled vegetables.

tips: Add the stock a splash at a time while mashing, because the beans thicken quickly as they cool and a loose mash at the stove ends up spoonable on the plate rather than stiff.
Mash in the pan while the beans are still hot, as the starch breaks down more easily and gives a creamier result with far less effort than mashing cold beans.
Squeeze the lime in at the very end, off the heat, since the acidity cuts through the earthy beans and stays bright instead of cooking off.
variations: Swap the neutral oil for bacon fat and fry a couple of chopped rashers with the onion for a smoky, richer pot of beans.
Use black beans instead of pinto and stir in 1 tsp smoked paprika with the cumin for a deeper, smokier flavour that suits burrito bowls.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Chinese Garlic Bok Choy
summary: Tender bok choy quickly stir-fried with garlic and a light savoury sauce.

stages.title: Prepare greens
steps: Trim the ends of bok choy and wash carefully between leaves to remove grit.
Halve larger heads lengthwise so they cook evenly.

stages.title: Sizzle garlic
steps: Heat neutral oil in a wok over medium heat and add finely chopped garlic.
Stir 20–30 seconds until fragrant but not browned.

stages.title: Stir-fry greens
steps: Add bok choy stems first and toss for 2 minutes, then add leafy tops and water.
Cover briefly until stems are tender-crisp and leaves wilt.

stages.title: Season and serve
steps: Splash in soy sauce and sesame oil and toss quickly to coat.
Serve immediately while the greens are bright and crisp.

tips: Add the stems before the leafy tops, because stems take about twice as long to soften and the leaves would turn slimy if they went in together.
Cook the garlic only until fragrant, as browned garlic turns bitter and would overpower the delicate, mildly sweet bok choy.
Dry the washed bok choy well before it hits the wok, since excess water steams the greens and dilutes the garlic flavour instead of letting them sizzle.
variations: Swap the soy sauce for 1 tbsp oyster sauce for a glossier, slightly sweet finish that suits rice-based family dinners.
Add 2 tsp finely grated ginger with the garlic and a handful of sliced shiitake mushrooms with the stems for a more savoury, earthy side.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: French Green Beans Almondine
summary: Crisp-tender green beans tossed in browned butter and toasted almonds.

stages.title: Blanch beans
steps: Boil beans in salted water for 3–4 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp.
Drain and plunge into cold water, then dry well.

stages.title: Toast almonds
steps: Toast almonds in a dry frying pan over medium heat, shaking frequently.
Remove as soon as lightly golden so they do not burn.

stages.title: Make browned butter
steps: Melt butter in the pan and cook until it smells nutty and turns pale golden.
Add finely chopped shallot and cook 1 minute, lowering heat if butter darkens.

stages.title: Toss and serve
steps: Add beans and toss until hot, then squeeze in lemon juice.
Scatter toasted almonds over the top and serve straight away.

tips: Dry the blanched beans thoroughly after the cold plunge, because leftover water makes the browned butter spit and stops it coating the beans.
Shock the beans in cold water straight after draining. This halts the cooking so they stay bright green and snappy rather than turning olive and soft.
Tip the almonds onto a plate as soon as they turn golden, because they keep colouring in the hot pan and will taste bitter if left in while you brown the butter.
variations: Swap the flaked almonds for toasted hazelnuts, roughly chopped, for a deeper, sweeter nuttiness that suits the browned butter.
Replace the lemon juice with a splash of white wine vinegar and stir through a spoonful of capers for a sharper, briny finish.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Italian Polenta with Parmesan
summary: Creamy soft polenta enriched with butter and Parmesan for a comforting Italian side.

stages.title: Heat liquids
steps: Bring stock and milk to a gentle simmer in a heavy saucepan.
Season lightly, remembering Parmesan will add salt later.

stages.title: Whisk in polenta
steps: Pour polenta in a slow stream while whisking continuously to prevent lumps.
Reduce heat and stir according to packet instructions until thick and tender.

stages.title: Enrich the polenta
steps: Turn off heat and stir in butter and finely grated Parmesan.
Add a splash of hot water or milk if too stiff; it should flow slowly from a spoon.

stages.title: Serve hot
steps: Taste for salt and add freshly ground pepper.
Spoon into warm bowls immediately before it firms up.

tips: Pour the polenta in a slow, steady stream while whisking so each grain is coated in liquid before it can clump, which gives a smooth, creamy finish.
Stir in the Parmesan off the heat so the cheese melts into the polenta rather than turning stringy or greasy, and so it stays glossy.
Keep a kettle of hot water or warm milk nearby, because polenta keeps thickening as it sits and cold liquid will cool it and dull the texture.
variations: Spread the cooked polenta in a lined tray, chill until firm, then cut into squares and pan-fry in olive oil for crisp-edged polenta cakes that suit grilled meat or roast vegetables.
Stir in a spoonful of mascarpone and a small handful of grated provolone or fontina instead of some of the Parmesan for a richer, creamier, more melting texture.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Turkish Ezme Salad
summary: Finely chopped tomato, pepper and onion tossed with parsley, chilli and pomegranate molasses.

stages.title: Chop vegetables
steps: Finely dice tomatoes, capsicum, onion and chilli into very small pieces.
Drain excess tomato juice to avoid a watery salad.

stages.title: Make dressing
steps: Whisk tomato paste, lemon juice, olive oil and pomegranate molasses.
Taste for a sharp, savoury balance and add a pinch of salt.

stages.title: Combine and rest
steps: Mix vegetables with dressing and finely chopped parsley.
Rest in the fridge for 10 minutes so flavours mingle.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Stir and taste again, adjusting lemon if necessary.
Serve with grilled meats, hummus or warm flatbread.

tips: Salt the diced tomatoes and let them drain in a sieve for a few minutes before dressing. This pulls out excess juice so the ezme stays thick and scoopable rather than turning into a watery puddle.

Dice everything very finely, close to the size of a pea. Small pieces release just enough juice to bind with the tomato paste and pomegranate molasses, and every spoonful gets a balanced mix of flavours.
Soak the chopped red onion in cold water for a couple of minutes and drain well. This takes the harsh raw bite off the onion so it doesn't overpower the sweet-tart molasses.
variations: Stir through a handful of finely chopped walnuts for a crunchy, nutty twist, similar to the Antep-style ezme served with kebabs.
Swap the red capsicum for a roasted one and add a teaspoon of Aleppo pepper (pul biber) for a smoky, mellow heat instead of the fresh green chilli.
storage: Refrigerate up to 2 days. Best eaten fresh; do not freeze.

title: American Fluffy Banana Pancakes
summary: Thick, fluffy banana pancakes with caramelised edges and naturally sweet fruit flavour.

stages.title: Mash bananas
steps: Mash ripe bananas with a fork until mostly smooth, leaving a few small lumps.
Whisk in eggs, milk, vanilla and cooled melted butter.

stages.title: Mix batter
steps: Combine flour, baking powder, sugar and salt in another bowl.
Fold wet ingredients into dry just until combined; small lumps are fine.

stages.title: Cook pancakes
steps: Heat a lightly buttered nonstick skillet over medium-low heat.
Cook 60 ml portions for 2–3 minutes until bubbles form, flip and cook 1–2 minutes until centres are set.

stages.title: Serve warm
steps: Keep cooked pancakes warm under a clean tea towel while finishing the batch.
Serve with sliced banana and yoghurt or maple syrup.

tips: Use bananas with plenty of brown spots: they are sweeter and mash more smoothly, so the pancakes taste of banana without needing extra sugar.
Stop folding while the batter is still a little lumpy. Overmixing develops gluten and makes the pancakes tough and flat instead of fluffy.
Keep the heat at medium-low and wait for bubbles before flipping. The banana sugars caramelise and burn quickly, and a hotter pan browns the outside before the thick centre sets.
variations: Fold 1/3 cup of dark chocolate chips or chopped walnuts into the batter for a banoffee-style stack.
Swap 50 g of the plain flour for wholemeal flour and add 1/2 tsp cinnamon for a nuttier, warmly spiced pancake.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Turkish Simit Breakfast Sandwich
summary: Toasted sesame bread rings filled with cheese, tomato, cucumber and fresh herbs.

stages.title: Prepare fillings
steps: Slice tomatoes and cucumber thinly and crumble feta into a bowl.
Split simit horizontally and toast lightly if desired.

stages.title: Cook eggs
steps: Heat olive oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat.
Fry eggs until whites are fully set and yolks reach your preferred doneness.

stages.title: Assemble sandwiches
steps: Layer tomato, cucumber and feta on the bottom halves of the simit.
Add cooked eggs and a little chopped parsley.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Close sandwiches gently so fillings do not spill.
Serve immediately while the bread is crisp and eggs warm.

tips: Toast the simit cut-side down in a dry pan or sandwich press: the sesame crust stays chewy outside while the cut face crisps up, which stops the tomato juices turning the base soggy.
Salt the sliced tomato and cucumber lightly and rest them on paper towel for a few minutes; this draws out excess water so the sandwich doesn't go limp before it reaches the table.

Crumble the feta by hand rather than slicing it, and pat it dry first. Small, dry crumbs sit in the bread better and the salty tang spreads through each bite, so you don't need extra salt on the eggs.
variations: Swap the fried eggs for soft scrambled eggs with a little butter; they stay put inside the ring and are easier for kids to eat.
Make it a Turkish-style kahvalti sandwich by spreading the base with kaymak or labneh and adding sliced black olives and a drizzle of honey for a sweet-savoury finish.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Japanese Tamagoyaki Omelette
summary: A delicately layered Japanese rolled omelette with a tender texture and subtle savoury sweetness.

stages.title: Mix eggs
steps: Beat eggs gently with dashi, soy sauce, sugar and salt until combined.
Strain if you want a particularly smooth omelette texture.

stages.title: Cook first layer
steps: Heat a small nonstick pan over medium-low and wipe with a thin film of oil.
Pour in a thin layer of egg and tilt pan to coat evenly.

stages.title: Roll in layers
steps: When nearly set, roll egg toward one edge with a spatula.
Oil exposed pan, add more egg under the roll and repeat until mixture is used.

stages.title: Shape and slice
steps: Rest rolled omelette for 2 minutes to finish setting.
Slice into thick pieces and serve warm with rice or pickles.

tips: Keep the heat at medium-low and lift the pan off the burner if the egg bubbles; browning makes the omelette tougher and spoils the pale yellow layers.
Strain the egg mixture through a sieve so stray bits of white don't leave streaks or holes, giving a smooth, even surface on each layer.
Rest the rolled omelette for a couple of minutes, or press it gently in a bamboo mat, so the layers fuse and it holds together when you cut thick slices.
variations: Make dashimaki tamago by increasing the dashi to 4 tablespoons and omitting the sugar; it's juicier and more savoury, but also more delicate to roll.
Lay a sheet of toasted nori or a strip of cheddar across the egg before rolling each layer for a spiral through the centre.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Indian Masala Dosa with Potato Filling
summary: Crisp fermented rice-lentil crêpes wrapped around warmly spiced potatoes and onions.

stages.title: Cook potato filling
steps: Boil peeled potato chunks until tender, then drain and roughly mash.
Heat 1 tbsp oil, pop mustard seeds, add onion, chilli, curry leaves and turmeric, and soften.

stages.title: Finish filling
steps: Fold mashed potatoes into the spiced onion and season with salt.
Add a splash of water if dry; filling should be moist but not runny.

stages.title: Cook thin dosas
steps: Heat a flat nonstick skillet and lightly oil it, then spread a ladle of batter in a thin spiral.
Cook until the underside is golden and edges lift, adding a few drops of oil around the rim.

stages.title: Fill and fold
steps: Place warm potato mixture along the centre of each dosa.
Fold over and serve immediately with coconut chutney or sambar.

tips: Wipe the hot pan with a halved onion or a lightly oiled cloth between dosas; this keeps the surface just greased enough for the batter to spread thinly without tearing or sticking.
Spread the batter in quick outward spirals as soon as it hits the pan, because it sets within seconds and a thin, even layer is what gives the crisp, lacy texture.
Mash the potatoes only roughly and let the filling cool slightly before spooning it in; chunky pieces keep some texture and a slightly cooled filling won't soften the crisp dosa.
variations: Make a paneer masala dosa by folding 150 g crumbled paneer through the potato filling with a pinch of garam masala for a more protein-rich breakfast.
Swap half the potato for cooked peas and diced carrot for a veggie-packed filling that suits kids, and leave out the green chilli.
storage: Refrigerate filling up to 3 days and batter according to its label. Cook dosas fresh for crispness.

title: Mexican Breakfast Chilaquiles Rojos
summary: Crisp tortilla pieces coated in red salsa, topped with eggs, crema and fresh cheese.

stages.title: Make red salsa
steps: Cook chopped onion, garlic and jalapeño in 1 tbsp oil until soft.
Add tomatoes and simmer 8 minutes, then blend until smooth and season with salt.

stages.title: Warm the chips
steps: Pour salsa into a wide pan and bring to a gentle simmer.
Fold tortilla chips through for 1–2 minutes, leaving some edges crisp.

stages.title: Cook eggs
steps: Heat remaining oil in a separate nonstick pan over medium heat.
Fry eggs until whites are fully set, keeping yolks soft if preferred.

stages.title: Assemble
steps: Divide saucy chips between plates and top each with an egg.
Scatter crumbled cheese and coriander over the top and serve at once.

tips: Fold the chips through the salsa for only 1–2 minutes and serve straight away, because the chips keep a little bite only while the salsa is hot and thick; any longer and they turn to mush.
Simmer the blended salsa for a minute or two if it looks thin, since a thicker salsa clings to the chips instead of pooling on the plate and soaking them.
Leave the seeds in the jalapeño for a hotter salsa or scrape them out for a milder, family-friendly version, as the seeds and white pith hold most of the heat.
variations: Swap the red salsa for salsa verde made with tomatillos (or green tomatoes), coriander and lime to make chilaquiles verdes, which are tangier and fresher.
Stir shredded leftover roast chicken through the salsa with the chips, then top with the egg for a heartier, protein-packed brunch.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: British Scrambled Eggs on Toast
summary: Soft, buttery scrambled eggs piled onto golden toast with a sprinkle of chives.

stages.title: Prepare eggs
steps: Crack eggs into a bowl and whisk until yolks and whites are just blended.
Season lightly and add milk if using.

stages.title: Toast bread
steps: Toast sourdough until golden while warming a nonstick pan over low heat.
Butter toast lightly if desired and keep warm.

stages.title: Scramble gently
steps: Melt butter over low heat, pour in eggs and stir slowly with a silicone spatula.
Lift the pan from heat briefly whenever curds set too quickly; stop while still glossy and softly set.

stages.title: Serve immediately
steps: Spoon eggs over toast and finish with black pepper and chives.
Eat straight away because residual heat continues to firm the eggs.

tips: Keep the heat low and stir slowly so the egg proteins set into small, creamy curds rather than tight, rubbery ones.
Pull the pan off the heat while the eggs still look slightly wet and glossy, because residual heat in the pan and the eggs will keep cooking them on the way to the table.
Salt the eggs just before they hit the pan rather than letting them sit, as salt left too long in the bowl can thin the eggs and make them a bit watery once cooked.
variations: Stir in 2 tbsp of cream cheese or mascarpone at the end for extra-rich, tangy eggs, and serve with thin slices of smoked salmon on top.
Fold through a handful of grated sharp cheddar and a teaspoon of Dijon mustard off the heat for a cheesy, Welsh rarebit-style scramble on toast.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: French Buckwheat Galettes with Egg and Cheese
summary: Nutty buckwheat crêpes folded around melted cheese, ham and a softly cooked egg.

stages.title: Make batter
steps: Whisk buckwheat flour, water, one egg and salt into a thin smooth batter.
Rest for at least 10 minutes to hydrate the flour.

stages.title: Cook galettes
steps: Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium and brush with butter.
Pour a thin layer of batter, swirling quickly, and cook until edges lift.

stages.title: Add fillings
steps: Flip each galette, crack an egg into the centre and scatter cheese and ham around it.
Cover briefly until egg white is set and cheese melts.

stages.title: Fold and serve
steps: Fold four sides inward to frame the egg while leaving the yolk visible.
Slide onto a plate and serve immediately.

tips: Rest the batter for at least 10 minutes, or overnight in the fridge if you have time: buckwheat flour absorbs water slowly, and a rested batter gives a more pliable galette that is less likely to tear when you flip it.
Make the first galette a test run and keep the pan at a steady medium heat: buckwheat batter cooks darker and faster than plain flour crêpes, so a too-hot pan burns the edges before the centre sets.
Crack each egg into a small cup first, then slide it onto the flipped galette: this lets you place the egg precisely in the centre and keeps stray shell out, so the folded square frames a runny yolk.
variations: Swap the ham and Gruyère for sautéed mushrooms, baby spinach and goat's cheese for a vegetarian galette; squeeze the spinach dry first so it doesn't make the base soggy.
Try a smoked salmon version: fill with Gruyère and egg as usual, then add smoked salmon, a spoonful of crème fraîche and dill after folding so the salmon stays silky rather than cooked.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Australian Bircher Muesli
summary: Creamy soaked oats with grated apple, yoghurt, nuts and a touch of lemon.

stages.title: Soak oats
steps: Mix oats, milk and yoghurt in a bowl until fully moistened.
Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight to soften.

stages.title: Prepare fruit
steps: Grate apple just before serving and toss with lemon juice to prevent browning.
Wash berries and drain well.

stages.title: Combine
steps: Stir grated apple and honey through the softened oats.
Add a splash of milk if the mixture has thickened too much.

stages.title: Finish bowls
steps: Divide into bowls and top with berries and chopped almonds.
Serve chilled, adding extra yoghurt if desired.

tips: Soak the oats overnight rather than for just a few hours, because the longer rest fully softens the rolled oats and lets them absorb the milk and yoghurt for a creamy, spoonable texture instead of a chewy one.
Grate the apple with the skin on and stir it through just before serving, as the peel adds fibre and a little tartness while grating late keeps the apple crisp and stops the mixture turning watery.
Keep the almonds separate until serving and toast them briefly in a dry pan if you have a minute, since they stay crunchy against the soft oats and toasting brings out a deeper nutty flavour.
variations: Swap the milk and yoghurt for coconut milk and coconut yoghurt, and top with toasted shredded coconut and mango for a dairy-free tropical version.
Replace the apple and berries with grated pear, a spoonful of stewed rhubarb and a pinch of cinnamon for a cosy winter bircher.
storage: Refrigerate covered up to 2 days. Add fresh fruit and nuts just before serving.

title: Vietnamese Fresh Spring Rolls
summary: Fresh rice paper rolls packed with herbs, crunchy vegetables and noodles, served with dipping sauce.

stages.title: Prepare fillings
steps: Cook vermicelli according to packet, rinse cool and drain thoroughly.
Julienne cucumber and carrot; wash and dry lettuce and herbs.

stages.title: Make dipping sauce
steps: Whisk hoisin and peanut butter with a few tablespoons of warm water until pourable.
Taste and adjust with lime juice if desired.

stages.title: Roll carefully
steps: Dip one rice paper sheet briefly in warm water and place on a damp board.
Layer lettuce, noodles, vegetables, herbs and cooked prawns, then fold sides inward and roll firmly.

stages.title: Serve fresh
steps: Arrange rolls apart so wrappers do not stick together.
Serve immediately with peanut dipping sauce.

tips: Dip each rice paper in warm water for only a few seconds; it keeps softening on the board, and over-soaked sheets turn gluey and tear when rolled.
Dry the lettuce, herbs and rinsed vermicelli thoroughly, because excess water makes the wrapper slippery and soggy, so the rolls won't seal tightly.
Place the prawns (halved lengthways if large) against the wrapper just above the lettuce so they show through the translucent paper, and keep the filling modest so the roll closes without splitting.
variations: Swap the prawns for shredded poached chicken or thinly sliced firm tofu pan-fried until golden for a different protein.
Make a nut-free dipping sauce by mixing hoisin with lime juice, a little water and finely chopped chilli, which suits school lunchboxes with nut restrictions.
storage: Best eaten immediately. Refrigerate assembled rolls up to 1 day tightly covered; texture will soften. Keep dipping sauce chilled.

title: Italian Panzanella Salad
summary: Juicy ripe tomatoes, crusty bread and basil tossed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.

stages.title: Prepare bread
steps: Tear day-old bread into bite-size pieces and toast briefly if very soft.
The bread should be firm enough to absorb dressing without disintegrating.

stages.title: Chop vegetables
steps: Cut tomatoes and cucumber into irregular chunks and thinly slice red onion.
Salt tomatoes lightly and collect their juices in the serving bowl.

stages.title: Make dressing
steps: Whisk vinegar with olive oil and black pepper, then combine with tomato juices.
Taste and adjust acidity so it tastes bright but not harsh.

stages.title: Toss and rest
steps: Add bread and vegetables to dressing and toss gently.
Rest 10–15 minutes, then fold in torn basil just before serving.

tips: Salt the chopped tomatoes and let them sit in the bowl for a few minutes before dressing: the salt draws out their juices, which become the base of the dressing and soak into the bread for far more flavour.
Use properly stale, crusty sourdough or ciabatta, and toast it briefly if it's still soft. A firm crumb soaks up the dressing and stays chewy, while soft sandwich bread turns to mush.
Soak the sliced red onion in the vinegar for 5 minutes before tossing everything together. This takes the raw bite out of the onion and keeps it from overpowering the tomatoes.
variations: Add a drained tin of cannellini beans and a few torn slices of prosciutto or some grilled chicken to turn it into a more filling main meal.
Swap the red onion for thinly sliced fennel, and add a handful of pitted Kalamata olives and capers for a saltier, more Sicilian-style panzanella.
storage: Best eaten fresh. Refrigerate leftovers up to 1 day; bread will become soft.

title: Mexican Black Bean Quesadillas
summary: Golden tortillas filled with seasoned black beans and melted cheese, served with fresh salsa.

stages.title: Prepare filling
steps: Drain and rinse beans, then lightly mash half with a fork.
Mix beans with diced capsicum, cumin, paprika and a squeeze of lime.

stages.title: Assemble tortillas
steps: Spread filling over one half of each tortilla, leaving a border.
Scatter cheese over the beans and fold tortillas closed.

stages.title: Toast quesadillas
steps: Heat a lightly oiled skillet over medium heat.
Cook each quesadilla 2–3 minutes per side until golden and cheese melts.

stages.title: Slice and serve
steps: Rest quesadillas for a minute before cutting into wedges.
Serve with salsa, yoghurt or sliced avocado.

tips: Mash about half the beans so they act as a sticky paste that holds the capsicum and cheese in place, which stops the filling sliding out when you flip.
Cook over medium heat rather than high: the tortilla needs the full 2-3 minutes per side to crisp up while the cheese melts through, and high heat will scorch the outside before the middle is hot.
Drain and rinse the beans well, then pat the diced capsicum dry if it's very juicy, as excess liquid makes the tortilla soggy instead of crisp.
variations: Swap the cheddar for a Mexican-style blend or pepper jack, and stir a diced jalapeño into the bean mix for a spicier, creamier quesadilla.
Add 1 cup of corn kernels and a handful of baby spinach to the filling, or use sweet potato mash instead of half the beans for a heartier version.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Japanese Soba Noodle Salad
summary: Chilled soba noodles tossed with crunchy vegetables and a sesame-soy dressing.

stages.title: Cook noodles
steps: Boil soba according to packet instructions, stirring early to prevent sticking.
Drain and rinse under cold water until cooled and excess starch washes away.

stages.title: Prepare vegetables
steps: Julienne cucumber and carrot into thin matchsticks.
Cook edamame until hot, then cool quickly and drain.

stages.title: Mix dressing
steps: Whisk soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil and honey until combined.
Taste for a salty-sour balance and adjust with a splash of water.

stages.title: Toss and serve
steps: Combine noodles, vegetables and edamame with dressing, lifting gently.
Scatter sesame seeds on top and serve chilled or at room temperature.

tips: Rinse the cooked soba under cold running water while gently rubbing the noodles, because this removes the surface starch that makes them gluey and clumpy once dressed.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan for a minute or two until golden, as the heat brings out their nutty flavour so they stand up to the soy and vinegar.
Dress the salad just before serving, since soba keeps absorbing the dressing and the cucumber releases water, which leaves the noodles soggy and the flavour diluted if it sits.
variations: Make it a heartier lunch by topping each bowl with sliced poached chicken or marinated firm tofu, and add a soft-boiled egg for extra protein.
Swap the sesame-soy dressing for a peanut-style one by whisking in 1 tbsp of smooth peanut butter with a squeeze of lime, and add shredded red cabbage for crunch.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Middle Eastern Falafel Wraps
summary: Warm flatbread wrapped around crisp falafel, pickles, vegetables and tahini sauce.

stages.title: Blend falafel mix
steps: Drain chickpeas soaked overnight and dry thoroughly; do not cook them first.
Pulse with onion, garlic, herbs and spices until finely crumbly, not puréed.

stages.title: Chill and shape
steps: Mix in baking powder and refrigerate the mixture 30 minutes.
Form small compact patties, pressing firmly so they hold together.

stages.title: Fry falafel
steps: Heat 2 cm oil to about 175°C in a deep pan and fry in batches until deep golden.
Drain on kitchen paper and check centres are cooked through.

stages.title: Build wraps
steps: Warm flatbreads and spread with tahini yoghurt sauce.
Add falafel, lettuce, tomato and pickles and roll tightly.

tips: Use soaked raw chickpeas, not canned or pre-cooked ones. Canned chickpeas hold too much water and turn the mix to mush, so the patties fall apart in the oil.
Pulse the mix to a coarse crumb that clumps when squeezed. Puréeing releases starch and gives dense, pasty falafel instead of a light, crisp-edged centre.
Keep the oil around 175°C and fry in small batches. Hotter oil browns the outside before the centre cooks, and overcrowding drops the temperature so the falafel soak up oil.
variations: Bake instead of frying: brush the patties with oil and bake at 220°C for about 25 minutes, turning once, for a lighter version with a less crisp crust.
Swap half the chickpeas for soaked dried broad beans (fava beans) for a greener, more traditional Egyptian-style falafel with a fluffier centre.
storage: Refrigerate cooked falafel up to 3 days or freeze up to 2 months. Reheat in a hot oven until steaming hot; assemble wraps fresh.

title: French Niçoise Salad
summary: Tuna, green beans, potatoes, eggs and olives arranged with tomatoes and mustard vinaigrette.

stages.title: Cook potatoes and eggs
steps: Boil potatoes in salted water until tender, then drain and halve.
Boil eggs to your preferred doneness, cool in cold water and peel.

stages.title: Blanch beans
steps: Cook beans in boiling salted water for 3–4 minutes until tender-crisp.
Transfer to cold water, then drain and pat dry.

stages.title: Make dressing
steps: Whisk olive oil, Dijon mustard and lemon juice until emulsified.
Season lightly, remembering tuna and olives already contain salt.

stages.title: Arrange salad
steps: Layer lettuce, potatoes, beans, tomatoes, tuna and olives on a platter.
Quarter eggs, arrange on top and spoon dressing over just before serving.

tips: Dress the potatoes while they're still warm, because warm potatoes soak up the mustard vinaigrette instead of just being coated by it, which seasons them all the way through.
Plunge the beans into cold water straight after blanching so they stop cooking and keep their bright green colour and snap.
Boil the eggs for about 7 minutes for jammy yolks that act like a second dressing, but cool them straight away so the yolks don't turn grey and chalky.
variations: Swap the tinned tuna for seared fresh tuna steaks, cooked rare for 1 minute each side and sliced over the salad for a more restaurant-style version.
Add anchovy fillets, thinly sliced red onion and a few capers for a more traditional Provençal flavour, and skip the extra salt in the dressing.
storage: Refrigerate components separately up to 2 days. Assemble fresh; do not leave egg or tuna unrefrigerated.

title: Korean Bibimbap Vegetable Bowls
summary: Steamed rice topped with colourful seasoned vegetables, sesame and spicy gochujang.

stages.title: Cook rice
steps: Rinse rice until water runs nearly clear and cook according to packet instructions.
Keep covered and warm while preparing toppings.

stages.title: Cook vegetables separately
steps: Julienne carrots and courgette and slice mushrooms thinly.
Sauté each in a little oil until tender, and blanch spinach briefly before squeezing dry.

stages.title: Make sauce and eggs
steps: Mix gochujang with sesame oil, soy sauce and a splash of water.
Fry eggs until whites are fully set and yolks reach desired doneness.

stages.title: Assemble bowls
steps: Divide rice among bowls and arrange vegetables in separate colourful sections.
Top with eggs and serve sauce on the side for mixing at the table.

tips: Squeeze the blanched spinach dry in your fist or a clean tea towel, because leftover water pools in the bowl and dilutes the gochujang sauce.
Cook each vegetable separately in the same pan, starting with the carrot and finishing with the mushrooms, so each keeps its own colour and texture instead of turning into a soggy stir-fry.
Leave a thin layer of rice in a hot, oiled pan for a couple of minutes before serving, as the crisp golden base mimics dolsot bibimbap and adds a satisfying crunch.
variations: Swap the eggs for marinated tofu: pan-fry firm tofu cubes in soy sauce and a little sesame oil until golden for a vegan bowl, and serve with the gochujang sauce thinned with water.
Add thinly sliced beef rump or lean mince marinated in soy, garlic and a little sugar, then stir-fried hot and fast, for a more traditional meaty bibimbap.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: British Coronation Chicken Sandwiches
summary: Tender chicken in a lightly curried, creamy dressing with mango chutney and crunchy greens.

stages.title: Make curry dressing
steps: Mix mayonnaise, yoghurt, curry powder, mango chutney and lemon juice until smooth.
Taste and adjust sweetness and acidity before adding chicken.

stages.title: Prepare chicken
steps: Shred chilled cooked chicken into bite-sized pieces, removing any gristle.
Fold into the dressing with raisins until evenly coated.

stages.title: Assemble sandwiches
steps: Lay lettuce on four bread slices to keep the bread from becoming soggy.
Spoon chicken mixture evenly over lettuce and top with remaining bread.

stages.title: Slice and serve
steps: Press sandwiches gently and cut into triangles with a sharp knife.
Serve chilled and keep refrigerated until eating.

tips: Shred the chicken rather than dicing it so the dressing clings to the strands and every bite is evenly coated.
Lay the lettuce directly on the bread as a barrier, because the moist filling will turn wholemeal slices soggy within about 30 minutes.
Chop any large pieces of mango chutney finely before mixing, so the sweet fruit pieces spread through the dressing instead of landing in one bite.
variations: Swap the raisins for halved red grapes and add toasted flaked almonds for a fresher, crunchier filling.
Serve the filling in a split baked jacket potato or on crisp cucumber rounds for a lighter, gluten-free option.
storage: Refrigerate chicken filling up to 2 days. Assemble sandwiches close to serving and keep chilled.

title: Turkish Lentil Köfte (Mercimek Köftesi)
summary: Soft red lentil and bulgur patties flavoured with tomato paste, cumin and fresh herbs.

stages.title: Cook lentils
steps: Rinse lentils and simmer in 550 ml water until soft and most liquid is absorbed.
Stir in fine bulgur, cover off the heat and rest 15 minutes until grains soften.

stages.title: Cook onion paste
steps: Fry finely diced onion in olive oil until golden.
Stir in tomato and pepper pastes and cumin, cooking 2 minutes to remove raw flavour.

stages.title: Mix and shape
steps: Combine lentil mixture with onion paste, lemon juice and chopped parsley.
When cool enough to handle, knead gently and form small oval patties.

stages.title: Serve in lettuce
steps: Arrange patties on crisp lettuce leaves with lemon wedges.
Serve at room temperature, squeezing lemon over just before eating.

tips: Rest the bulgur off the heat in the hot lentils rather than boiling it: the residual steam softens the grains without turning the mixture gluggy, so the patties hold their shape.
Fry the tomato and pepper pastes for a full 2 minutes before mixing in, because it caramelises their sugars and removes the tinny edge, giving a deeper, rounder flavour.
Knead the mixture while it's still slightly warm: the starch from the lentils and bulgur is stickier then, so the patties bind without any egg or flour.
variations: Swap the pepper paste for 1 tbsp pomegranate molasses and add a few chopped spring onions for a tangier, sharper köfte.
Pack the mixture into a wrap with cucumber, shredded cabbage and a smear of yoghurt for a more filling lunchbox option.
storage: Refrigerate promptly up to 3 days. Serve chilled or at room temperature briefly; do not freeze lettuce.

title: Italian Tiramisu Cups
summary: Individual layers of espresso-soaked sponge and mascarpone cream, finished with cocoa.

stages.title: Make mascarpone cream
steps: Whip cold cream with icing sugar and vanilla to soft peaks.
Fold in mascarpone gently until smooth, avoiding overbeating.

stages.title: Prepare coffee biscuits
steps: Pour cooled coffee into a shallow dish and break biscuits to fit four glasses.
Dip biscuits briefly, about 1 second per side, so they absorb coffee without collapsing.

stages.title: Layer desserts
steps: Place soaked biscuits in glasses and spoon over a layer of mascarpone cream.
Repeat layers and smooth the tops with a spoon.

stages.title: Chill and dust
steps: Refrigerate cups for at least 2 hours so the layers set and flavours meld.
Dust with cocoa just before serving to keep the surface dry.

tips: Fold the mascarpone into the whipped cream rather than beating it in, because mascarpone splits and turns grainy when overworked, which ruins the silky layers.
Dip the savoiardi for only a second per side, as they are very dry and keep soaking in the fridge; a longer dunk leaves a soggy, watery base once chilled.
Dust the cocoa just before serving, since cocoa left on the cream for hours absorbs moisture and turns blotchy and damp.
variations: Swap the coffee for cooled strong chai or hot chocolate and use a splash of Marsala or Frangelico in the dip for a boozy, nutty version for adults.
Make a berry tiramisu cup by dipping the biscuits in a mix of cooled orange juice and a little Grand Marnier, then layering with sliced strawberries and raspberries instead of coffee flavours.
storage: Refrigerate covered up to 2 days. Do not leave at room temperature for prolonged periods.

title: French Crème Brûlée
summary: Smooth vanilla custard beneath a brittle, caramelised sugar crust.
ingredients: 1 vanilla bean or 2 tsp vanilla paste
40 g extra caster sugar for topping

stages.title: Heat cream
steps: Heat oven to 150°C conventional and warm cream with vanilla until steaming, not boiling.
Remove from heat and let infuse for 5 minutes.

stages.title: Mix custard
steps: Whisk yolks and 80 g sugar until combined but not foamy.
Slowly pour warm cream into yolks while whisking to avoid scrambling, then strain.

stages.title: Bake in water bath
steps: Divide custard among four ramekins and place in a deep roasting tray.
Pour hot water halfway up ramekins and bake 35–40 minutes until edges set but centres wobble.

stages.title: Chill and caramelise
steps: Cool, then refrigerate at least 2 hours until cold and firm.
Sprinkle thin even sugar layers and caramelise with a kitchen torch immediately before serving.

tips: Pour the hot water into the roasting tray after it's on the oven rack, so you don't slosh water into the custards. The water bath keeps the oven heat gentle and even, which stops the yolks curdling and gives a silky set.

Pull the ramekins out while the centres still wobble like set jelly. The custard keeps cooking from residual heat and firms up fully as it chills, so waiting for a firm centre in the oven leads to a grainy, overcooked texture.
Pat any condensation off the chilled custards with paper towel before sugaring. Moisture on the surface dissolves the sugar into a syrup instead of letting it melt into a glassy, crackly crust.
variations: Swap the vanilla for 2 tbsp of finely grated orange zest and a splash of Grand Marnier, infusing the zest in the warm cream, for a citrus crème brûlée that cuts through the richness.
Infuse the warm cream with 2 tbsp of good loose-leaf Earl Grey tea for 5 minutes, then strain before mixing with the yolks, for a fragrant, bergamot-scented custard.
storage: Refrigerate uncaramelised custards covered up to 2 days. Caramelise just before serving.

title: British Apple Crumble
summary: Tender baked apples with cinnamon beneath a buttery golden crumble topping.

stages.title: Prepare fruit
steps: Heat oven to 190°C conventional and peel, core and slice apples evenly.
Toss with caster sugar, cinnamon and lemon juice, then spread in a baking dish.

stages.title: Make crumble topping
steps: Rub cold butter into flour until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs.
Stir in brown sugar and oats, leaving a few larger buttery clumps.

stages.title: Bake until bubbling
steps: Scatter crumble evenly over apples without pressing it down.
Bake 30–35 minutes until topping is golden and fruit bubbles around the edges.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Rest crumble 10 minutes so the juices thicken slightly.
Serve warm with custard, cream or vanilla ice cream.

tips: Use Granny Smith or another firm cooking apple, because they hold their shape and their tartness balances the sweet topping, whereas Pink Lady or Gala can collapse into mush.
Keep the butter cold and leave some pea-sized clumps in the topping, as these melt slowly in the oven and create a crisp, crunchy crumble rather than a flat, greasy layer.
Scatter the crumble over the apples without pressing it down so steam can escape; compacting it traps moisture and makes the underside of the topping soggy.
variations: Swap half the apples for blackberries or rhubarb, adding an extra 2 tbsp of caster sugar for the rhubarb, for a tarter, more colourful filling.
Replace 30 g of the flour with chopped roasted hazelnuts or almond meal for a nuttier, extra crunchy topping.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Japanese Dorayaki Pancakes
summary: Soft Japanese pancakes sandwiched around sweet red bean paste.

stages.title: Whisk batter
steps: Whisk eggs, sugar and honey until pale and lightly thickened.
Sift in flour and baking powder, then stir in water until smooth.

stages.title: Rest batter
steps: Cover batter and rest 10 minutes so bubbles settle.
Heat a lightly oiled nonstick pan over low-medium heat.

stages.title: Cook rounds
steps: Pour small equal circles of batter and cook until bubbles appear on top.
Flip gently and cook the second side briefly until golden; cool on a rack.

stages.title: Sandwich filling
steps: Spread red bean paste over the underside of half the pancakes.
Top with remaining pancakes, press edges gently and serve.

tips: Whisk the eggs, sugar and honey until pale and thick, because that trapped air is the only lift besides the baking powder and it gives the pancakes their soft, spongy crumb.
Keep the pan on low-medium heat and wipe it with a thin film of oil between batches; this gives an even golden face, whereas a hot pan scorches the sugary batter before the centre sets.
