Cool the pancakes on a rack before filling, or the warm surface will soften the bean paste and the steam will make the pancakes soggy.
variations: Swap the red bean paste for chestnut spread or sweet white bean paste for a milder, nuttier filling.
Fill with whipped cream and sliced strawberries for a lighter, fresher take that suits warmer weather.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Indian Cardamom Rice Pudding (Kheer)
summary: Creamy rice pudding perfumed with cardamom, saffron and toasted nuts.

stages.title: Rinse and soak rice
steps: Rinse rice until water runs mostly clear and soak in cool water for 10 minutes.
Drain thoroughly and lightly crush cardamom pods.

stages.title: Simmer milk and rice
steps: Bring milk to a gentle simmer in a heavy pot, then add rice and cardamom.
Cook over low heat 40–45 minutes, stirring often to prevent scorching, until rice is very tender.

stages.title: Sweeten and enrich
steps: Stir in sugar and raisins and continue simmering until creamy.
Add rose water if using and remove cardamom pods where practical.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Spoon into bowls and scatter chopped pistachios over the top.
Serve warm or chill thoroughly for a cold pudding.

tips: Use a heavy-based pot and keep the heat low: milk scorches on the bottom easily over the 40+ minutes of simmering, and a burnt layer taints the whole pudding with a bitter flavour.
Soaking the rice for 10 minutes lets the grains absorb water so they soften evenly and release starch gradually, which gives the kheer its creamy body.
Add the sugar only once the rice is completely tender, because sugar slows softening and the grains can stay firm if it goes in too early.
variations: Swap the rice for 80 g of broken vermicelli (seviyan) and cook for only 10 to 15 minutes for a quicker kheer.
Replace half the milk with a 400 ml can of coconut milk and use almonds instead of pistachios for a richer, tropical-style pudding that is also lovely chilled.
storage: Cool promptly and refrigerate up to 2 days. Reheat thoroughly with a splash of milk; do not leave cooked rice at room temperature.

title: American Baked New York Cookies
summary: Thick bakery-style cookies with golden edges, soft centres and generous chocolate chunks.

stages.title: Cream butter and sugars
steps: Heat oven to 180°C conventional and line two baking trays.
Beat softened butter with both sugars until fluffy, then mix in eggs and vanilla.

stages.title: Mix dough
steps: Whisk flour, baking soda and salt in a separate bowl.
Fold dry ingredients into butter mixture, then stir in chocolate chunks.

stages.title: Chill and portion
steps: Chill dough 20 minutes to reduce spreading.
Scoop into equal mounds, leaving generous space between cookies.

stages.title: Bake and cool
steps: Bake 11–14 minutes until edges are golden but centres still look slightly soft.
Cool on trays for 10 minutes before transferring to a rack.

tips: Chilling the dough for the full 20 minutes firms up the butter, so the cookies spread less in the oven and stay thick with soft centres instead of baking into flat discs.
Pull the trays out while the centres still look slightly underdone; the cookies keep cooking on the hot tray for those 10 minutes and set to a chewy middle rather than going dry and crisp.
Use roughly chopped chunks from a block of dark chocolate rather than chips, as the uneven pieces melt into pools and layers, giving the bakery-style look and a more intense chocolate hit.
variations: Brown the butter first and cool it until soft and solid again before creaming. This adds a nutty, toffee-like depth that pairs well with the dark chocolate.
Swap half the dark chocolate for roughly chopped walnuts or macadamias and finish each cookie with a few flakes of sea salt for a salty-sweet crunch.
storage: Keep airtight up to 4 days or freeze baked cookies up to 2 months. Raw dough balls freeze well.

title: Portuguese Pastéis de Nata
summary: Flaky Portuguese custard tarts with blistered tops and crisp buttery pastry.

stages.title: Prepare pastry cases
steps: Heat oven to 240°C conventional and roll puff pastry tightly into a log.
Slice into 12 pieces and press each into a greased muffin tin, working from centre outward.

stages.title: Cook syrup and milk
steps: Simmer sugar, water, cinnamon and lemon peel for 3 minutes, then remove aromatics.
Whisk flour with a little cold milk, add remaining milk and heat until lightly thickened.

stages.title: Make custard
steps: Slowly whisk hot syrup into the milk mixture, then let cool slightly.
Whisk in egg yolks and strain to remove lumps before filling pastry shells three-quarters full.

stages.title: Bake until blistered
steps: Bake 12–16 minutes until pastry is crisp and custard tops develop dark caramelised spots.
Cool 10 minutes before removing from tins; serve warm.

tips: Roll the pastry log tightly and press each slice out from the centre with wet thumbs, so the base stays thin and the sides rise into a crisp, flaky cup rather than a doughy one.

Use the hottest oven you can (240°C) and bake near the top: the intense heat blisters the custard and caramelises the sugar into the signature dark spots before the filling overcooks and turns rubbery.
Strain the custard through a fine sieve after adding the yolks, as this catches any cooked egg or flour lumps and gives a silky, smooth filling.
variations: Swap the lemon peel for a strip of orange peel and add a drop of vanilla extract for a softer, more fragrant custard.
Make them Macanese-style by using less sugar syrup and baking at a slightly lower temperature, which gives a lighter, more eggy custard with a golden top and less char.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.

title: Greek Orange and Yoghurt Cake
summary: Moist Greek yoghurt cake with fresh orange zest and a fragrant citrus syrup.

stages.title: Prepare cake tin
steps: Heat oven to 180°C conventional and grease a 22 cm round cake tin.
Line the base with baking paper and finely zest oranges without white pith.

stages.title: Mix wet ingredients
steps: Whisk yoghurt, sugar, eggs, olive oil, vanilla and orange zest until smooth.
Add 80 ml fresh orange juice and whisk briefly.

stages.title: Fold and bake
steps: Fold in flour and salt gently until no dry pockets remain.
Pour into tin and bake 35–40 minutes until a skewer inserted in centre comes out clean.

stages.title: Cool and serve
steps: Cool in tin 10 minutes, then turn out onto a rack.
Serve with extra yoghurt and a little orange zest.

tips: Zest the oranges before juicing them, and avoid the white pith: it's bitter, while the zest oils carry the fragrant citrus flavour through the crumb.
Fold the flour in gently and stop as soon as no dry pockets remain, because overmixing develops gluten and makes an olive oil cake dense rather than tender.
Use a mild extra virgin olive oil, as a very peppery one can turn bitter against the orange; the oil is what keeps the cake moist for days.
variations: Make it a syrup cake: simmer 100 ml orange juice with 60 g sugar until slightly thickened, then spoon it over the warm cake so it soaks in.
Swap one orange for 2 lemons' worth of zest and juice, and add 2 tbsp poppy seeds for a Greek-style lemon and poppy seed cake.
storage: Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat cooked components until steaming hot; keep crisp garnishes separate.
